## Findings
- claim-1: For \(J=[333,5^5]\), \(Q=J/A_+J\) has free ranks \(1,1,2,2,2,1,1\) in degrees \(9,\ldots,15\), vanishes thereafter through degree \(25\), and has no torsion. [artifact b5658ec18b84ad470751544a752f238dadd447fb7b1122a89a299a79e024042f]
- claim-2: The lower-adjoined Schur family \(\{\bar s_\mu: i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 220-235]
- claim-3: **Basis criterion.** If homogeneous generators \(F\) generate \(J\), and \(Q=J/A_+J\) is torsion-free with \(\operatorname{rank}Q_d=\#F_d\) for every \(d\), then the images of \(F_d\) are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q_d\). Indeed, they give a surjection \(\mathbb Z^{\#F_d}\twoheadrightarrow Q_d\) between free groups of equal rank, hence an isomorphism.
- claim-4: For the computed case \(i=j=b=3,\ a=2\), the criterion explains the accepted data: the generator enumerator is \(z^9\binom52_z\), so \(\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9\binom52_z\).
- claim-5: Minimality alone cannot imply the basis criterion: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(J=(2x,x^2)\), the two generators are minimal, but \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\{2x\}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)\{x^2\}\).
## Strategy
Use the single symbolic invariant \(Q=J/A_+J\).

**Lemma.** If homogeneous \(F\) generates \(J\), \(Q\) is torsion-free, and \(\operatorname{rank}Q_d=\#F_d\) for every \(d\), then the images of \(F_d\) form a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(Q_d\).

Indeed, \(\mathbb Z^{\#F_d}\twoheadrightarrow Q_d\) is a surjection between free abelian groups of equal rank, so its kernel has rank \(0\); as a subgroup of a free abelian group it is free, hence zero.

For \([333,5^5]\), the accepted computation gives torsion-free \(Q\) with ranks
\[
(1,1,2,2,2,1,1)
\]
in degrees \(9,\ldots,15\), zero through degree \(25\), and
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_Q(z)=z^9\binom52_z.
\]
This equals the degree enumerator of the source-backed generating family. Thus the lemma explains the accepted finite data without further computation.

The requested strategy-pivot target is established via this single indecomposables-basis criterion; the original finite Hilbert-series target remains established only for \([333,5^5]\), while the proposed universal inference from minimality is not established.

## Gaps
Minimality alone does not imply the lemma’s torsion-free hypothesis. Precisely,
\[
A=\mathbb Z[x],\qquad J=(2x,x^2)
\]
has a minimal two-element generating family, but
\[
J/A_+J\cong \mathbb Z\{2x\}\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)\{x^2\}.
\]
Hence no uniform Hilbert-series or integral-basis conclusion follows from minimality without separate torsion and rank control.

## Next
A generalization would require a symbolic proof of torsion-freeness and the degreewise rank formula for \(J/A_+J\); the accepted finite computation does not supply this.
